acceptance.given: The published policy, contract schema, result schema, standard, and reference package are available from repository-owned paths for validation.

oracle.expected: A structured validation result confirms one shared declared version and identical rule-vocabulary identifiers across the policy, both schemas, the standard, and the reference package.
forbidden: Any version mismatch among the policy, schemas, standard, and reference package.
Any rule-vocabulary mismatch, missing rule, or extra rule among those artifacts.
oracle.observable: The validator or contract test compares normalized version and rule-vocabulary values across all required artifacts and reports a distinct alignment outcome.

acceptance.then: The validation artifact records the cross-artifact comparison and identifies any divergence as a structured failure.
acceptance.when: During artifact validation, execute the frozen version-and-rule-vocabulary alignment check against the actual repository artifacts.

failure_intents.selector_intent: scripts/sc/tests/test_skill_quality_core.py::test_a04 presents a policy, schema, standard, or reference artifact with a divergent declared version or rule vocabulary and asserts that the real validator returns a structured failure identifying the mismatch.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Provide deterministic cross-artifact validation that accepts aligned version and rule vocabulary and rejects divergence with structured diagnostics.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Revert only the validator and normative artifact changes for this alignment rule; preserve sidecar and package schema compatibility and require aligned version and rule vocabulary before acceptance.

slice_hint.state_transition: Alignment transitions from unestablished to validated when all declared versions and normalized rule identifiers match; any divergence transitions to deterministic validation failure.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The whole-plan pytest selection executes the alignment assertion and the validator result confirms matching version and rule vocabulary for the reference package while rejecting a divergent mutation.
